Explanation: To humbly negate or disagree with what someone has said.
Korean Sentence 1: 한국말을 잘 하기는요. 쉬운 말밖에 못 해요.
English Sentence 1: I'm not good at Korean. I can only speak simple phrases.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 한국말을 참 잘하시네요.
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 잘 하기는요. 아직도 모르는 게 많아요.
English Sentence 2A: A: You're so good at Korean.
English Sentence 2B: B: Not at all. There are so many things I still don't know.

Explanation: To state that something is "only" or "just" the case, with nothing more.
Korean Sentence 1: 건강이 좋아진 특별한 방법은 없어요. 아침마다 산책을 했을 뿐이에요.
English Sentence 1: There isn't any secret method to my health improving. All I did was take a walk every morning.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 영수씨, 얼굴이 안 좋아 보여요. 어디 아프세요?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 괜찮아요. 좀 피곤할 뿐이에요.
English Sentence 2A: A: Yeongsu, you don't look well. Are you sick?
English Sentence 2B: B: I'm okay. I'm just tired.

Explanation: To express the purpose or intent for doing something ("in order to").
Korean Sentence 1: 저는 세계 여행을 하기 위해서 외국어를 공부해요.
English Sentence 1: I am learning a foreign language in order to travel the world.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 우디씨, 왜 그렇게 열심히 공부해요?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 공무원 시험에 합격하기 위해서 열심히 공부해요.
English Sentence 2A: A: Woody, why are you studying so hard?
English Sentence 2B: B: I am studying hard in order to pass the civil service examination.

Explanation: To describe something in relative terms, avoiding a definitive statement ("to be on the relatively... side").
Korean Sentence 1: 플릭 씨는 키가 큰 편이지요.
English Sentence 1: Flick is pretty tall.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 날이 이렇게 더운데 집까지 30분이나 걸어가야 해요. 너무 멀어요.
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 그 정도면 가까운 편이지요. 저는 한 시간 이상 걸려요.
English Sentence 2A: A: It's so hot and I have to walk 30 minutes to get home. It's too far.
English Sentence 2B: B: That's pretty close. It takes me more than an hour to get home.

Explanation: To express that you were just about to do something.
Korean Sentence 1: 저도 지금 점심을 먹으려던 참이었어요.
English Sentence 1: I was just about to eat lunch, too.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 3시 기차를 타려면 지금 출발해야 될 것 같은데요.
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 그렇지 않아도 이제 출발하려던 참이었어요.
English Sentence 2A: A: I think we need to leave now in order to board the 3 o'clock train.
English Sentence 2B: B: As a matter of fact, I was just about to leave.

Explanation: To indicate that someone "only" does that action and nothing else.
Korean Sentence 1: 아이가 밥도 안 먹고 울기만 해요.
English Sentence 1: The baby doesn't even eat and only cries.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 어머니께서 요리를 하실 때 마리아 씨도 같이 했어요?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 아니요, 저는 옆에서 보기만 했어요.
English Sentence 2A: A: Did you help your mother with the cooking, Maria?
English Sentence 2B: B: No, I just watched from the side.

Explanation: To express that someone "must" or "should" do something.
Korean Sentence 1: 약속을 했으면 지켜야지요.
English Sentence 1: If you make a promise, you need to keep it.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 영수 씨가 저에게만 한 이야기를 실수로 다른 사람에게 말했어요.
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 비밀 이야기는 다른 사람에게 말하지 말아야지요.
English Sentence 2A: A: I accidentally spilled the beans on the secret that Yeongsu only shared with me.
English Sentence 2B: B: You shouldn't tell others a secret (that's been told to you).

Explanation: Used with a descriptive verb to say someone/something "looks" a certain way.
Korean Sentence 1: 흐엉 씨는 나이보다 어려 보여요.
English Sentence 1: Huong, you look younger than your age.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 이 영화가 재미있어 보이는데 우리 이 영화를 볼까요?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 좋아요. 저도 보고 싶었던 거예요.
English Sentence 2A: A: This movie looks fun. Do you want to watch it?
English Sentence 2B: B: Sure. I've been wanting to watch it, too.

Explanation: To make a hypothetical supposition about something ("if... were to happen").
Korean Sentence 1: 만약 10억이 생긴다면 집을 사고 싶어요.
English Sentence 1: If I got a billion dollars, I would want to buy a house.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 뭐든지 만들 수 있다면 뭘 만들고 싶어요?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 뭐든지 만들 수 있다면 젊어지는 약을 만들고 싶어요.
English Sentence 2A: A: If you could make anything, what would you want to make?
English Sentence 2B: B: If I could make anything, I would want to make a potion that makes people younger.

Explanation: To suggest a possible reason for something ("Perhaps it's because...").
Korean Sentence 1: 요즘 과로해서 그런지 자주 머리가 아파요.
English Sentence 1: Perhaps it's because I'm overworked these days, but my head frequently hurts.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 존 씨는 참 똑똑한 것 같아요.
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 책을 많이 읽어서 그런지 아는 것이 많아요.
English Sentence 2A: A: I think John is very smart.
English Sentence 2B: B: Perhaps it's because he reads a lot, but he's well-informed.

Explanation: The passive voice, where the subject is acted upon.
Korean Sentence 1: 도둑이 경찰에게 잡혔어요.
English Sentence 1: The thieves were caught by the police.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 제 이야기가 잘 들리세요?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 잘 안 들려요. 좀 더 크게 말씀해 주세요.
English Sentence 2A: A: Can you hear me?
English Sentence 2B: B: Your voice can't be heard clearly. Please speak louder.

Explanation: To indicate the state that remains after an action has been completed.
Korean Sentence 1: 책상 위에 교과서가 놓여 있었어요.
English Sentence 1: The textbook was on the desk.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 윤아야, 내 모자가 어디에 있지?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 저기 옷걸이에 걸려 있어.
English Sentence 2A: A: Yuna, where's my hat?
English Sentence 2B: B: It's hanging on the coat rack over there.

Explanation: To express thoughts about choosing between options ("whether to... or...").
Korean Sentence 1: 저는 친구 결혼식 때 원피스를 입을지 바지를 입을지 생각 중이에요.
English Sentence 1: I'm still deciding whether to wear a dress or slacks to my friend's wedding.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 링링 씨, 졸업 후에 뭘 할 거예요?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 대학원에 갈지 일을 할지 아직 결정하지 못했어요.
English Sentence 2A: A: Ling Ling, what are you going to do after you graduate?
English Sentence 2B: B: I haven't decided yet whether to go to graduate school or get a job.

Explanation: To indicate an action is completed and its result is being maintained for later use.
Korean Sentence 1: 시원하게 마시려고 냉장고에 음료수를 넣어 놓았어요.
English Sentence 1: I've put the beverage in the refrigerator so I can drink it cold.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 내일이 노라 씨 생일인데 케이크는 준비했어요?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 네, 제가 만들어 놓았어요.
English Sentence 2A: A: Tomorrow is Nora's birthday. Have you prepared the cake?
English Sentence 2B: B: Yes, I've baked it.

Explanation: The shortened form for reported speech ("He/she said...").
Korean Sentence 1: 에릭 씨가 다음 달에 고향에 돌아간대요.
English Sentence 1: Eric says he's going to return to his hometown next month.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 유키 씨가 왜 아직 안 오지요?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 아까 연락이 왔는데 조금 늦는대요.
English Sentence 2A: A: Why isn't Yuki here yet?
English Sentence 2B: B: She called a little while ago and said she was going to be a bit late.

Explanation: Used with ~나/나 to mean "anyone," "anything," "anytime," etc.
Korean Sentence 1: 목이 마르니까 마실 것이 있으면 아무거나 주세요.
English Sentence 1: I'm so thirsty. If you have anything to drink, please give it to me.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 내일 파티에 무슨 옷을 입고 가야 돼요?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 중요한 자리가 아니니까 아무 옷이나 입어도 돼요.
English Sentence 2A: A: What do I need to wear to tomorrow's party?
English Sentence 2B: B: It's not an important event, so just wear anything.

Explanation: To state a realization or outcome resulting from a past action.
Korean Sentence 1: 제가 오랜만에 고향에 갔더니 친구들이 모두 떠나고 없었어요.
English Sentence 1: Because I visited my hometown for the first time in a long time, all my friends had all left.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 에릭 씨, 어디 아프세요?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 며칠 과로했더니 병이 났어요.
English Sentence 2A: A: Eric, are you feeling sick?
English Sentence 2B: B: I got sick because I overworked myself for a few days.

Explanation: To remind or confirm something the listener already knows ("As you know...").
Korean Sentence 1: 레오 씨가 요리를 잘하잖아요.
English Sentence 1: (As you know) Leo is a good cook.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 왜 이렇게 열심히 공부해요?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 다음 주에 시험이 있잖아요.
English Sentence 2A: A: Why are you studying so diligently?
English Sentence 2B: B: (As you know) There's a test next week.

Explanation: To indicate that one action happens "after" another is completed.
Korean Sentence 1: 저는 어제 영화를 보고 나서 늦게 저녁을 먹었어요.
English Sentence 1: After watching a movie yesterday, I ate a late dinner.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 엄마, 저 한 시간만 게임해도 돼요?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 숙제 먼저 다 하고 나서 게임해라.
English Sentence 2A: A: Mom, can I play games for just one hour?
English Sentence 2B: B: Play your game after you finish your homework.

Explanation: To ask for confirmation about something you heard ("Is it true that...?").
Korean Sentence 1: 요즘 이튼 씨 회사에서 드라마를 찍는다면서요?
English Sentence 1: Is it true that a drama series is being filmed at your company these days, Ethan?
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 우리 학교에 '남자친구들'이 공연하러 온다면서요?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 네, 저도 아까 들었어요. 정말 기대가 돼요.
English Sentence 2A: A: Is it true that "Boyfriends" is coming to perform at our school?
English Sentence 2B: B: Yes, I heard that, too. I'm so excited.

Explanation: To express "even though" or "despite" something.
Korean Sentence 1: 저는 날마다 운동을 하는데도 건강이 별로 좋아지지 않아요.
English Sentence 1: Even though I exercise every day, my health is not improving.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 오늘은 날씨가 정말 춥지요?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 네, 두꺼운 코트를 입고 있는데도 추워서 몸이 떨려요.
English Sentence 2A: A: It's really cold today, isn't it?
English Sentence 2B: B: Yes. Even though I'm wearing a thick coat, it's still cold so I'm shivering.

Explanation: Attached to a verb to mean "it is easy to..."
Korean Sentence 1: 계절이 바뀌는 때에는 감기에 걸리기가 쉬워요.
English Sentence 1: It's easy to catch a cold when the seasons change.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 요즘 회사 일 때문에 너무 바빠서 동창회 날짜를 잊어버렸어.
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 바빠서 기억을 못했구나. 잊어버리기가 쉬운 날짜는 메모해 놓는 게 좋아.
English Sentence 2A: A: I've been so busy at work lately that I forgot the date of our reunion.
English Sentence 2B: B: Oh I see. You forgot because you were so busy. You should write down dates that are easy to forget.

Explanation: To express uncertainty or possibility ("might" or "may").
Korean Sentence 1: 날씨가 추운데 친구가 밖에서 기다릴지도 몰라서 서둘러서 나왔어요.
English Sentence 1: I rushed just in case my friend might be waiting outside in the cold.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 올리비아 씨가 계속 전화를 안 받아요.
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 자고 있을지도 몰라요.
English Sentence 2A: A: Olivia isn't picking up her phone.
English Sentence 2B: B: She might be sleeping.

Explanation: Used with verbs of change to plan for a future point in time ("In order for it to be...").
Korean Sentence 1: 밥이 다 되려면 10분 남았다.
English Sentence 1: There are 10 minutes left until the rice is ready.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 저기요, 저희가 주문한 음식은 언제 나오나요?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 죄송합니다. 오늘 손님이 많아서 음식이 나오려면 좀 더 기다리셔야 합니다.
English Sentence 2A: A: Excuse me, when will our food be ready?
English Sentence 2B: B: I'm sorry. We have a lot of customers today, so you'll have to wait a little longer for your food to come out.

Explanation: Used when listing examples ("... or something like that").
Korean Sentence 1: 비빔밥이라든가 삼계탕 같은 한국 음식이 건강에 좋아요.
English Sentence 1: Korean foods like bibimbap or samgyetang are good for the health.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 일요일 오후에는 보통 뭘 하세요?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 빨래라든가 청소 같은 집안일을 해요.
English Sentence 2A: A: What do you usually do on Sunday afternoon?
English Sentence 2B: B: I usually do household chores like the laundry or cleaning.

Explanation: To make a speculation about a past event ("must have," "probably").
Korean Sentence 1: 지금 3시니까 영화가 끝났을 거예요.
English Sentence 1: It's 3 p.m, so the movie is probably over already.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 메리 씨가 소포를 받았겠지요?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 보통 미국까지 나흘 정도 걸리잖아요. 아직 못 받았을 거예요.
English Sentence 2A: A: Mary probably received the package, right?
English Sentence 2B: B: It usually takes four days for a delivery to be made to the U.S. I don't think she received it yet.

Explanation: To make an assumption based on visual evidence ("It looks like...", "I guess...").
Korean Sentence 1: 노라 씨에게 연락했는데 전화를 안 받아요. 벌써 자나 봐요.
English Sentence 1: I called Nora, but she wouldn't pick up. Maybe she's already sleeping.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 식당 앞에 사람들이 길게 줄을 서 있어요.
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 이 식당 음식이 정말 맛있나 봐요.
English Sentence 2A: A: There's a long line in front of that restaurant.
English Sentence 2B: B: The food there must be really delicious.

Explanation: To formally state one's opinion ("I think that...").
Korean Sentence 1: 저는 리에 씨가 잘못했으니까 리에 씨가 먼저 사과해야 한다고 생각해요.
English Sentence 1: I think that Rie needs to apologize first because she's the one who made the mistake.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 열심히 공부하는데도 한국어 실력이 늘지 않아서 걱정이야.
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 혼자 공부하는 것도 좋지만 한국 사람들과 많이 이야기하는 게 중요하다고 생각해.
English Sentence 2A: A: I'm worried because my Korean isn't improving, even though I'm studying hard.
English Sentence 2B: B: I think it's good to study alone, but it's more important that you talk to a lot of Korean people.

Explanation: To indicate doing one thing "instead of" another, or "in return for" something.
Korean Sentence 1: 시간이 없어서 극장에 가는 대신에 집에서 영화를 봤어요.
English Sentence 1: I didn't have time, so instead of going to the theater, I watched a movie at home.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 우리 언어 교환을 할까요?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 좋아요, 리에 씨가 저에게 일본말을 가르쳐 주는 대신에 저는 리에 씨에게 한국말을 가르쳐 드릴게요.
English Sentence 2A: A: Should we do a language exchange?
English Sentence 2B: B: Sounds good. In return for you teaching me Japanese, Rie, I'll teach you Korean.

Explanation: The causative form, meaning "to make/let someone do something."
Korean Sentence 1: 친구가 저를 화나게 했어요.
English Sentence 1: My friend made me angry.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 우리 아이가 게을러서 걱정이에요.
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 아이가 스스로 방을 청소하게 하세요. 그럼 부지런해질 거예요.
English Sentence 2A: A: I'm worried because my child is so lazy.
English Sentence 2B: B: Make him clean his own room. Then, he will become more industrious.

Explanation: To express a contrast between two actions or states by the same subject ("even while...").
Korean Sentence 1: 저는 과식이 건강에 안 좋은 줄 알면서도 항상 많이 먹어요.
English Sentence 1: I know that overeating is bad for the health, but I always eat a lot.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 노라 씨, 언니하고 또 싸웠어요?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 싸우면 안 되는 줄 알면서도 화가 나서 참지 못했어요.
English Sentence 2A: A: Nora, did you fight with your sister again?
English Sentence 2B: B: I know I shouldn't, but I just can't keep my anger in.

Explanation: To provide background information based on personal experience before giving advice, making a suggestion, or asking a question.
Korean Sentence 1: 미선 씨, 민주 백화점에서 세일을 하던데 같이 갈래요?
English Sentence 1: Miseon, I saw Minju Department Store is having a sale. Would you like to go?
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 오랜만에 친구를 보기로 했는데 어디에서 만나면 좋을까?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 지하철 역 앞에 커피숍이 새로 생겼던데 거기에 가 봐.
English Sentence 2A: A: I decided to see my friend for the first time in a long time. Where should I meet him?
English Sentence 2B: B: There's a new coffee shop in front of the subway station. Give it a try.

Explanation: To indicate a sequence of actions, emphasizing the first action is done before the second ("and then").
Korean Sentence 1: 카드를 넣고서 비밀번호를 누르세요.
English Sentence 1: Put in your card and then input your PIN.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 미선 씨, 왜 그래요? 발이 아파요?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 네, 어제 구두를 신고서 오래 걸었더니 발이 아파요.
English Sentence 2A: A: Miseon, what's the matter? Does your foot hurt?
English Sentence 2B: B: Yes, I wore heels and walked for a long time yesterday, so my foot hurts.

Explanation: To express that something almost happened ("nearly," "almost").
Korean Sentence 1: 길이 막혀서 약속 시간에 늦을 뻔했어요.
English Sentence 1: There was so much traffic that I was almost late to my appointment.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 웨이 씨가 사고가 나서 병원에 입원했다면서요?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 네, 조금만 늦게 병원에 갔으면 큰일 날 뻔했대요.
English Sentence 2A: A: I heard that Wei got into an accident and is in the hospital.
English Sentence 2B: B: Yes, they say that if she had arrived at the hospital a few minutes late, it would have been dangerous.

Explanation: The causative form, where the subject makes someone else perform an action.
Korean Sentence 1: 올리비아 씨가 차를 마시려고 물을 끓였어요.
English Sentence 1: Olivia boiled the water to drink tea.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 내일 아침에 일찍 일어나야 한다고 했지?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 네, 혹시 제가 못 일어나면 깨워 주세요.
English Sentence 2A: A: You said you need to wake up early in the morning tomorrow, right?
English Sentence 2B: B: Yes. If I don't wake up, please wake me up.

Explanation: To state that the second clause was discovered or realized as a result of the action in the first clause.
Korean Sentence 1: 떡볶이를 먹어 보니까 생각보다 안 매웠어요.
English Sentence 1: After eating tteokbokki, I realized it wasn't as spicy as I had thought it would be.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 한국 생활이 어때요?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 혼자 살아 보니까 생각보다 재미있어요.
English Sentence 2A: A: How is life in Korea?
English Sentence 2B: B: After living alone, I've realized it's more fun than I had expected.

Explanation: To express that something contrary to one's intention happened ("I was trying to... but...").
Korean Sentence 1: 커피에 설탕을 넣는다는 것이 소금을 넣었어요.
English Sentence 1: I was trying to put sugar in my coffee but happened to put salt in.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 소희야, 이게 누구 옷이니?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 어머, 제 옷을 챙긴다는 것이 미나 옷을 가지고 왔나 봐요.
English Sentence 2A: A: Sohee, whose clothes are these?
English Sentence 2B: B: Oh my. I was planning on bringing my clothes but brought Mina's clothes instead.

Explanation: To express that something ended up happening, often regrettably or unintentionally ("ended up V-ing").
Korean Sentence 1: 화가 나도 참아야 하는데 그만 화를 내고 말았어요.
English Sentence 1: I should have kept in my anger, but I happened to get angry.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 노라 씨가 왜 저렇게 화가 났어요?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 제가 친구들과 이야기하다가 실수로 노라 씨의 비밀을 말하고 말았어요.
English Sentence 2A: A: Why is Nora so angry?
English Sentence 2B: B: I was talking with my friends and happened to share Nora's secret.

Explanation: Used at the end of a sentence to provide a reason or explanation for a previous statement.
Korean Sentence 1: 누리 씨는 학교에서 인기가 많아요. 노래를 아주 잘하거든요.
English Sentence 1: Nuri is very popular at school because she is a good singer.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 케빈 씨, 무슨 일이 있어요?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 여자친구가 화가 많이 났어요. 제가 약속을 어겼거든요.
English Sentence 2A: A: Is something the matter, Kevin?
English Sentence 2B: B: My girlfriend is really mad because I broke a promise.

Explanation: To express worry or concern that something might happen ("I'm afraid that...").
Korean Sentence 1: 비가 올까 봐 우산을 가지고 왔어요.
English Sentence 1: Just in case it rains, I brought an umbrella.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 줄리 씨, 왜 이렇게 일찍 왔어요?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 길이 막힐까 봐 오늘은 집에서 일찍 출발했어요.
English Sentence 2A: A: Why did you come so early, Julie?
English Sentence 2B: B: I was afraid there would be traffic, so I left early from home today.
